This live session takes participants from an empty local DHIS2 instance
to a working malaria programme dashboard. The lesson covers the full
workflow: setting up the system, defining its metadata, entering and
checking data, calculating indicators, building visualizations, and
managing access.

::: {.callout-note title="Session and materials"}
- **Date and time:** September 30, 2026 at 12:00 UTC
- [Open the complete 18-topic lesson](../../11_dhis2/lesson/index.html)
- [Browse the session materials](https://github.com/AMMnet/ammnet-hackathon/tree/main/11_dhis2)
- [View the original lesson repository](https://github.com/mohamedsillahkanu/AMMnet-test-Hackathon)
:::

## Who this is for

This session is for public-health practitioners, monitoring and
evaluation teams, health-information-system administrators, and others
who want a practical introduction to configuring and using DHIS2. The
lesson begins with the core concepts and does not assume previous DHIS2
administration experience.

## What you will learn

By the end of the session, you will be able to:

1. Explain how DHIS2 represents aggregate and case-based health data.
2. Run a local DHIS2 instance with Docker and navigate its main apps.
3. Configure organisation units, data elements, category combinations,
   data sets, and data-entry forms.
4. Enter and validate aggregate and case-based data.
5. Define indicators and check their calculations.
6. Build tables, charts, thematic maps, and a programme dashboard.
7. Create users, export data, customize the system, and install apps.

## Before the session

To run DHIS2 locally, prepare:

- a Windows, macOS, or Ubuntu computer;
- [Docker Desktop](https://www.docker.com/products/docker-desktop/) or
  Docker Engine with at least 4 GB of memory assigned;
- about 5 GB of free disk space;
- [Git](https://git-scm.com/downloads) or the ability to download a ZIP;
  and
- a modern web browser.

The local setup uses DHIS2 2.42.1 with PostGIS. The first image download
is about 1 GB and can take several minutes, so complete it before the
session when possible. Topic 2 includes setup and troubleshooting
instructions for each supported operating system.

::: {.callout-warning title="CSV exercise files pending"}
Topic 3 describes an optional CSV route for importing organisation
units, but the referenced `orgunits_import.csv` and
`orgunit_groups_template.csv` files were not included in the supplied
repository. Participants can complete the organisation-unit exercise
manually. We will add the CSV files if they become available.
:::

## Session outline

The 18 topics build on one another:

1. **Understand and install DHIS2:** learn the data model and start a
   local instance.
2. **Build the metadata:** create organisation units, data elements,
   category combinations, a data set, and its entry form.
3. **Enter data:** work with aggregate and case-based records and design
   custom forms when needed.
4. **Turn data into information:** define indicators and create charts,
   maps, and a dashboard.
5. **Operate the system:** manage users, download data, customize DHIS2,
   and add apps from the App Hub.

## Training environment

The supplied Docker configuration is intended for local learning. A
production DHIS2 deployment requires secure credentials, HTTPS,
backups, monitoring, and an operational maintenance plan. Change the
default administrator password after the first login, even in the local
training instance.
